doc.title: Chick Corea — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Steve Swallow and the Sweet Rain record with Getz
summary: Steve Swallow mentors Corea and urges him to do Sweet Rain, where Getz recorded 'Litha' and 'Windows'.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I believe you told me that Steve Swallow was the one who referred you to Stan Getz?
Yes. I met Steve earlier in that playing in Pete LaRoca’s quartet with John Gilmore.

There’s a recording, Women At the Turkish Baths. Steve was another mentor of mine, and a great friend in helping me work my way through how to be a musician in New York. He was very friendly. He advised me, for instance, to go ahead and be on the Sweet Rain record. The original group for Sweet Rain was Roy Haynes and Steve Swallow, but then Stan didn’t want to use Roy on that gig for some reason, whatever, and because of that, Steve, in a group spirit, said, “well, I’m not going to be on the record either.” So then, in a group spirit, I said, “Well, I’m not going to be on the record either.” Then Steve called me up. He said, “No-no, Chick, you should go do that record. Stan is going to record some of your songs. This will be good for you.”
Yeah, “Litha” and another one we did on that record... “Windows.”
